table_title: List the 11 notable ship canals worldwide per Wikipedia's `Ship canal` master article's 'Notable ship canals' table, ordered by Length (km) DESC. Universe filter: rows in the closed `Notable ship canals` table (NOT broader 'List of canals' which includes irrigation/historical/leisure canals — pivoted per cycle-1 audit's BLOCKING #1). For each notable ship canal, give the Year Opened, Length in kilometers, Maximum Ship Dimensions (length × beam × draft in meters per master's compound cell format), and Route Endpoints (start point — end point per master's text format with country prefix where applicable). Note: Wikipedia master table includes 11 canals comprising the canonical 'notable ship canals' set as of cycle-1 audit's verbatim dump on 2026-05-19. NOT 'Major international' framing (renamed from initial proposal `major_international_ship_canals_by_length_km` per cycle-1 audit's BLOCKING fix — the master title is 'Notable ship canals' and several entries are domestic ship channels like Houston Ship Channel + Welland Canal).
db_analog: SELECT canal_name, year_opened, length_km, maximum_ship_dimensions_m, route_endpoints FROM wiki_ship_canal_notable_ship_canals_table ORDER BY length_km DESC
temporal_note: Wikipedia `Ship canal` master article's 'Notable ship canals' table, accessed via cycle-1 audit's master-derived 11-row dump on 2026-05-19. Universe is the closed canonical 11-entry 'Notable ship canals' table — NOT the broader `List of canals by country` (list-of-lists with country bullets, not uniform master table) NOR `List of waterways` (explicitly marked incomplete). source_count = 1 registered (Wikipedia `Ship canal` article — universe + value role for all 5 cells per master's compound table). Per cycle-1 audit's BLOCKING fix #1: source-plan pivoted from 'List of canals' (insufficient as master) to 'Ship canal' article's 'Notable ship canals' table (uniform 11-row table with canal name + year opened + length + maximum ship dimensions + start/end points). Per cycle-1 audit's BLOCKING fix #2: universe corrected to the 11 master-table rows exactly — my cycle-1 preview had 6 out-of-scope canals (Grand Canal, Erie Canal, Rideau Canal, Göta Canal, Albert Canal, Caledonian Canal) and missed 2 in-scope canals (Houston Ship Channel, Danube–Black Sea Canal); audit's master-derived dump committed verbatim. Per-row cells: Canal name verbatim from master table; Year Opened integer (note: Welland Canal Year Opened = 1932 reflects the current Fourth Welland Canal — the original Welland Canal opened 1829 but master table shows 1932); Length (km) numeric (longest = Saint Lawrence Seaway 600 km; shortest = Welland Canal 43.4 km — clears 10-row gate); Maximum Ship Dimensions (m) compound text format 'length x beam x draft' (e.g., '226 x 24 x 8' for Saint Lawrence Seaway; 'Unlimited x 78 x 20' for Suez Canal which has no length limit); Route Endpoints text format 'X: Start — End' with country prefix (em-dash separator). temporal_sensitivity = low — canal infrastructure doesn't change often; new notable ship canals are infrequent additions. Cycle-1 audit's required pivot from 'major international ship canals' to 'notable ship canals' applied at cycle-0 staging — ID renamed `major_international_ship_canals_by_length_km` → `notable_ship_canals_by_length_km`; schema columns aligned with master ('Maximum Ship Dimensions (m)' + 'Route Endpoints' per master's compound-cell formats); 11-row verbatim dump used.
